messages:
ingress-bot: Alert: spike detected on /v1/generate p99 = 2.3s, p95 = 1.1s for 10m window. Affected tenants: acme-inc, beta-co. link: https://metrics.internal/r/redwood/ingress

maya (support): Customer report — several API errors and timeouts starting ~03:12 UTC. They saw 504s and very slow responses. Provided sample request id: req_8a7f.

maya (support): Repro steps from customer: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -- they said a single request sometimes takes >2s.

rob (eng-runtime): Looking at ingress proxy panels — queue length spiked at the same time. I suspect admission-controller is throttling, but requests are not fast-failing. Can someone check recent deploys/config changes?

deploy-bot: Deployed commit 8f9a3c1 to infra/ratelimit at 2026-03-17T03:05:48Z by @alice. Change: default global concurrency cap lowered from 500 -> 50 in config flag `global_ingress_concurrency`.

carlos (eng-sre): That sounds... bad. If global cap dropped to 50 while traffic steady, workers will queue and p99 will explode. Also saw retries from some SDKs (auth token rotation morning job) adding burst. Combined effect = queueing overload.

oncall_jess: Quick mitigation I can do: bump global_ingress_concurrency back to 500, and enable fast-fail for unauthenticated requests. Which service owns the flag?

alice (eng-platform): That's infra/ratelimit -- I pushed the change. The intention was to protect backend but we missed staged rollout. Reverting now.

rob (eng-runtime): While that's rolling, can we short-circuit retries from the edge? Add 429 for over-limit and set Retry-After. Also temporarily lower max batch size so worker CPU isn't pegged.

carlos (eng-sre): Metrics after revert: queue length down 80% within 30s. p95 back near baseline in ~60s. We still see some noisy tenants (acme-inc) causing bursts. Suggest tenant-level caps and priority routing for enterprise customers.

maya (support): Customer notified that we identified a config rollback as root cause and reverted - apologised; they confirmed improvement. They asked for postmortem and any tenant mitigation.

alice (eng-platform): Action items: (1) postmortem noting bad default change + no gradual rollout; (2) add automated canary for concurrency flag changes; (3) implement tenant burst caps + quicker fast-fail path.

rob (eng-runtime): Repro command for internal testing (use debug token):
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H 'Authorization: Bearer debug-token' -d '{"input":"x"}' https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
```

carlos (eng-sre): Note: seen a related issue where SDKs retry on 401 during token rotation. We'll add jitter and exponential backoff limits in the SDK.

oncall_jess: Mitigation commands I ran:
```bash
# revert rate limit config
kubectl -n infra patch configmap ratelimit --patch '{"data":{"global_ingress_concurrency":"500"}}'
# set fast-fail header
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/ingress-proxy FAST_FAIL=true
```
Both applied at 03:12:40Z, rollout healthy.

maya (support): Closing loop with customer: they see normal p95 now, will watch p99 for 24h. Thanks team :thumbsup:

alice (eng-platform): I'll draft the postmortem and schedule a short runbook update for how to change global caps (must staged rollout + canary).

rob (eng-runtime): Follow-ups: add alert for sudden global cap changes, and dashboard for per-tenant retry storms.

ingress-bot: Note: no further spikes in the last 15m.
